lessons.title: Plans for Tomorrow
objectives: talk about immediate future plans
ask what someone is going to do
combine a plan with a time and place

teaching.explanation: The high-frequency future pattern is werden + infinitive: Ich werde lernen, du wirst arbeiten, er/sie wird essen. For near future German often also uses the present tense, but lernen the werden-form as a clear chunk for planning.
teaching.pattern: Ich werde morgen lernen. Was wirst du tun? = What are you going to do?
teaching.note: German does not repeat a short preposition the way Spanish does; use simple locative phrases like 'in Berlin' or 'ins Café' as appropriate.

examples.en: I am going to study tomorrow.
What are you going to do?
We are going to eat at eight.

activities.prompt: Choose “I am going to work.”
Translate: “What are you going to do tomorrow?”
Complete: Wir werden ___ um acht essen.
Put in order: lernen / morgen / Ich / werde
Say three plans for tomorrow using different verbs.
activities.answer: Morgen werde ich ____. Danach werde ich _____. Schließlich werde ich ____.

lessons.mission: Make and discuss a simple plan.

dialogue.title: Planning tomorrow

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: A
lines.de: Ich werde mich ausruhen.
lines.en: I am going to rest.

learner_turns: Make the plans realistic or imaginary.

exit_check: Build three immediate-future sentences.
Ask about another person’s plans.
Combine a plan with sequence and time.

lessons.title: Getting Around
objectives: ask where a place is
understand left, right, straight, and near
give a two-step direction

teaching.explanation: Direction language is best practiced with a map or visual route. Keep the sentence frame stable while changing only one landmark at a time. Use the formal imperative for polite directions (Gehen Sie geradeaus, Biegen Sie rechts ab); informally use du-forms with peers.
teaching.pattern: Wo ist die Bank? Gehen Sie geradeaus. Biegen Sie rechts ab. Es ist in der Nähe.
teaching.safety: For real-world safety, confirm important directions and use a map; this lesson is language practice, not navigation advice.

activities.prompt: Match: links = left; rechts = right; geradeaus = straight; in der Nähe = near.
activities.answer: links = left; rechts = right; geradeaus = straight; in der Nähe = near.

activities.prompt: Translate: “Where is the station?”
Choose “Turn right.”
Put in order: geradeaus / Gehen Sie / und / biegen / rechts / ab
activities.answer: Gehen Sie geradeaus und biegen Sie rechts ab.

activities.prompt: Give directions from a hotel to a café using two steps.
activities.answer: Gehen Sie geradeaus. Biegen Sie nach ___. Es ist in der Nähe.

lessons.mission: Navigate a short route while asking for clarification.

lines.speaker: A
lines.de: Danke.
lines.en: Thank you.

learner_turns: Give directions using a drawn route.

exit_check: Retrieve four direction words.
Ask for a place.
Give two connected direction steps.

lessons.title: Conversation Glue
objectives: connect ideas with y, pero, porque, también
clarify a word or ask for a slower repetition
give a short reason

teaching.explanation: Conversation becomes less robotic when sentences connect. Start with four glue words and use them repeatedly.
teaching.pattern: Ich mag Kaffee, weil er gut ist. Ich arbeite und studiere. Ich will keinen Tee, aber ich will Wasser.
teaching.repair: Was bedeutet ___? = What does ___ mean? Wie sagt man ___? = How do you say ___?

examples.de: Ich mag es, weil es gut ist.
examples.en: I like it because it is good.

activities.prompt: Match: und = and; aber = but; weil = because; auch = also.
activities.answer: und = and; aber = but; weil = because; auch = also.

activities.prompt: Translate: “I like tea because it is good.”
activities.answer: Ich mag Tee, weil er gut ist.

activities.prompt: Complete: Ich will keinen Kaffee, ___ ich will Tee.
Ask “What does ___ mean?” about the word in der Nähe.
Give a preference with a reason and one contrast.
activities.answer: Ich mag ____ weil ____. Ich mag ___ nicht, aber ____.

lessons.mission: Keep an imperfect conversation moving and make meaning clear.

dialogue.title: Clarifying a misunderstanding

lines.speaker: A
lines.de: Willst du Kaffee?
lines.en: Do you want coffee?

lines.speaker: B
lines.de: Ich verstehe nicht. Was bedeutet ‚Kaffee‘?
lines.en: I do not understand. What does café mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.de: Das ist ein Getränk.
lines.en: It is a drink.

lines.speaker: B
lines.de: Ah, ja. Ich möchte Kaffee, bitte.
lines.en: Ah, yes. I want coffee, please.

learner_turns: Use "Kannst du das wiederholen?" and "Was bedeutet ...?"

exit_check: Join two ideas with y or pero.
Give one reason with porque.
Use two repair strategies without switching languages.

lessons.title: High-Frequency Irregulars
objectives: recognize essential irregular forms
use tengo for possession and basic states
build practical sentences without overgeneralizing regular endings

teaching.explanation: Some of the most useful verbs are irregular. Learn the first-person forms as chunks: ich bin, ich habe, ich gehe, ich mache. Add the subject only when contrast or emphasis helps.
teaching.pattern: Ich habe Zeit. Ich bin müde. Ich gehe ins Café. Ich stelle eine Frage.
teaching.note: German adjectives like 'müde' do not change for gender in the same way; accept the basic form.

examples.en: I am going to the café.

activities.prompt: Write the five first-person chunks: I am (identity), I am (state/location), I have, I go, I do.
activities.answer: ich bin, ich bin, ich habe, ich gehe, ich mache

activities.prompt: Translate: “I have time.”
Choose the sentence for “I am tired” (speaker feminine allowed).
Complete: Ich gehe ___ Café.
Make five short sentences, one with each first-person chunk.
activities.answer: Ich bin ____. Ich bin ____. Ich habe ____. Ich gehe ____. Ich mache ____.

lessons.title: People, Places, and Plans
objectives: sustain a conversation for two minutes
ask follow-up questions
combine identity, routine, preference, and plans

teaching.explanation: Today trains conversation turns. A conversation is not a speech: answer, ask back, react, and repair. Use "Und du?" and "Was machst du gern?" to return the turn.
teaching.pattern: Ich komme aus ____. Ich wohne in ____. Ich arbeite und studiere. Ich mag ____. Morgen werde ich ____. Und du?
teaching.strategy: When stuck, use one of four moves: repeat, ask meaning, ask the partner a question, or give a simpler answer.

vocabulary.en: What do you like to do?

examples.en: What do you like to do?
Tomorrow I am going to work.

activities.prompt: Write a five-line self-profile from memory.
activities.answer: Ich heiße ____. Ich komme aus ____. Ich wohne in ____. Ich mag ____. Morgen werde ich ____.

activities.prompt: Listen to a learner profile and identify origin, routine, preference, and plan.
Order the conversation moves: answer / ask back / repair / close
Answer: Was machst du gern? Include a reason with weil.
Hold a two-minute conversation with four required moves.
activities.answer: Introduce yourself, ask a question, answer a preference, state a plan, and ask "Und du?"

lessons.mission: Sustain a short exchange by answering and asking back.

lessons.title: Listening and Comprehension
objectives: extract key facts from a short dialogue
use context to tolerate unknown words
respond to who, where, when, and what questions

teaching.explanation: Do not demand word-for-word comprehension. First listen for the mission facts: person, place, time, action. Then replay for details. This mirrors real listening, where the learner must act on meaning rather than translate every word.
teaching.pattern: Who? wer. Where? wo. When? wann. What? was. Why? warum.
teaching.strategy: Listen once for the situation, once for facts, and a third time for one useful phrase.

examples.en: When are you going to study?
I am going to study at home.

activities.prompt: After the first play, choose the main mission: meeting, shopping, or scheduling.
After the second play, identify the place.
After the second play, identify the time.
Write the phrase for “because I have time.”
Replay the dialogue and speak simultaneously with the audio, then repeat from memory.
activities.feedback: Completion is behavioral: the learner must shadow once and produce the key sentence without audio.

lessons.mission: Understand the actionable facts in a short slow dialogue.

dialogue.title: Listen, extract, act
dialogue.audio_script: Hallo. Morgen werde ich um acht zu Hause lernen, weil ich Zeit habe. Danach gehe ich arbeiten. Und du?
dialogue.translation: Hi. Tomorrow I am going to study at home at eight because I have time. Afterwards I am going to work. And you?

exit_check: Identify the main situation before translating.
Extract place, time, and reason.
Shadow and reproduce one sentence.

lessons.title: Week 4 Final Mission
objectives: understand and produce a simple conversation
form new sentences from known patterns
demonstrate a sustainable review habit

teaching.explanation: The final mission is a performance check. The learner must use German to meet someone, exchange personal information, describe a routine, express a preference, make a plan, ask for directions or help, and repair one misunderstanding.
teaching.success_definition: A successful beginner conversation is understandable, responsive, and resilient. It may contain errors; it must not depend on memorizing one exact script.
teaching.next_step: After Week 4, the learner should enter an A1 continuation course covering more present-tense verbs, direct objects, gender exceptions, past events, expanded listening, and regular speaking practice.

examples.en: My name is ____. I am from ____.

activities.prompt: From memory, write a seven-line self-introduction and plan.
activities.answer: Hallo. Ich heiße ____. Ich komme aus ____. Ich wohne in ____. Ich mag ____. Morgen werde ich ____. Und du?

activities.prompt: Listen to a final dialogue and answer who, where, what, when, and why.
Translate: “I need help. Where is the station? Can you repeat, please?”
activities.answer: Ich brauche Hilfe. Wo ist der Bahnhof? Können Sie das bitte wiederholen?

activities.prompt: Correct two errors in a short paragraph and explain the reason for each.
activities.feedback: The app should identify agreement, hay/estar, gustar, or word-order errors and show one concise explanation.

activities.prompt: Complete the final mission with a simulated partner for 3–5 minutes.
activities.feedback: Pass target: at least 80% task completion, at least two successful repair moves, and understandable responses to follow-up questions.

lessons.mission: Hold a flexible beginner conversation about familiar needs and plans.
